evals.prompt: Our adult users come back from /age-gate/check as 'unverified'. Build an in-app verification prompt and iframe modal to let them verify.
evals.expected_output: A verification prompt that opens an iframe modal (not a new tab) containing the verification URL; URL fetched on demand; polling plus wake triggers; idempotent success handler.
assertions: The verification URL is fetched on-demand when the modal opens, not prefetched at parent mount
The verification URL is rendered in an iframe inside a modal, not via window.open or target=_blank
verifyId is stored with useState (or equivalent reactive state), not useRef
Polling runs while the modal is open and wakes on visibilitychange and focus
Success handler is idempotent (guarded by a resolvedRef or equivalent)
Modal is closed BEFORE the session is refreshed
Session update is a single call path (not a local state clear followed by a refreshSession)

evals.expected_output: Body likely has top-level age or ageCategory; should be nested under criteria: { ageCategory: 'ADULT' }.
assertions: Response identifies the nested criteria.ageCategory body shape as the fix
Response notes top-level age fields are rejected with 400 in every pattern
Response links or references the endpoint's docs.k-id.com page

evals.prompt: Our user verified age in a new tab but our app never unlocked.
evals.expected_output: Diagnosis prescribes the three-strategy return-path detection: server poll + BroadcastChannel + visibility wake, run in parallel.
assertions: Response proposes at least server polling AND visibility-wake
Response mentions BroadcastChannel or a cross-tab detection mechanism
Response notes postMessage is a hint, not authoritative
Response explains why window.open is fragile on iOS Safari

evals.prompt: We're launching in Brazil. The ECA Digital rules require age 18 for loot-boxes. A permission in session.permissions has verifiedAgeThreshold: 18 and enabled: false. How do I gate the UI and unlock it?
evals.expected_output: Render the loot-box feature with a 'Verify your age' lock; on tap call /session/upgrade for that permission; handle CHALLENGE_SESSION_UPGRADE_BY_AGE_ASSURANCE by opening the iframe verification modal; on success, refresh the session and unlock.
assertions: Response distinguishes verifiedAgeThreshold from GUARDIAN-managed permissions
Response handles CHALLENGE_SESSION_UPGRADE_BY_AGE_ASSURANCE specifically (not the generic consent widget)
Response routes to the age-verification iframe modal, not the parental-consent modal
Response refreshes the session after successful verification
Response notes the permission can never be unlocked through parental consent

evals.prompt: UK Online Safety Act requires 'highly effective age assurance' for our 18+ site. We have user accounts and permissions per feature (restricted messaging, restricted social feed, etc). Integrate k-ID.
evals.expected_output: Full sessioned integration: age gate first, then either the unverified-adult verification path (if the adult site requires proving adult status before any feature) or the per-permission threshold path (if individual adult features have their own thresholds). Method selection happens server-side based on Compliance Studio jurisdiction settings; no client-side filtering of verification methods.
assertions: Response starts with the age gate (not age verification)
Response uses Pattern 2 (unverified adult) OR Pattern 3 (threshold), not standalone AgeKit+, because the product has sessioned features
Response does NOT hardcode a specific verification method (facial age estimation, ID doc, etc.)
Response notes that 'highly effective age assurance' is a Compliance Studio server-side setting, not a client flag
Response references docs.k-id.com for endpoint shapes rather than inventing them

evals.prompt: We have a simple 18+ site, no accounts, no persistent user state — just need to prove the user is 18+ once on entry. Integrate k-ID with the minimum code.
evals.expected_output: Standalone AgeKit+ (Pattern 1). Server-to-server call to /age-verification/perform-access-age-verification with { jurisdiction, criteria: { ageCategory: 'ADULT' } } and NO sessionId. Render url in an iframe. Act on PASS/FAIL via webhook or /age-verification/get-status?id=<id>. No age gate, no session, no permissions.
assertions: Response identifies this as Pattern 1 / standalone AgeKit+
Response does NOT include a sessionId in the request body
Response does NOT stand up an age gate, a session, or a permission-management UI
Response keeps the create-verification call server-side (api key protected)
Response shows reading the result via webhook OR /age-verification/get-status (not just postMessage)
Response does not invent a new endpoint; uses /age-verification/perform-access-age-verification

evals.prompt: A user abandoned our AgeKit+ verification flow yesterday and is back now trying again. What should our code do?
evals.expected_output: Check /age-verification/get-status?id=<id> first. If the previous verification is still valid (not expired — URLs are valid for 2 weeks), reuse it. If get-status returns 400 with INVALID_INPUT the verification is expired — create a new one by calling /age-verification/perform-access-age-verification again.
assertions: Response checks status of the prior verification before creating a new one
Response mentions the 2-week URL validity window
Response handles INVALID_INPUT by creating a fresh verification, not by retrying the old URL
Response does not suggest client-side rebuilding of the verification URL
